title: Cookies
definition: Small pieces of data sent by a web server and stored locally in the user's web browser. The browser automatically sends them back to the server with every subsequent request.
simpleExplanation: HTTP has 'amnesia' (it is stateless). If you log in, the server forgets who you are one second later. A Cookie is a nametag the server glues to your shirt. Every time you walk up to the server to ask for a new page, the server reads the nametag and says 'Ah, welcome back John.'
realWorldExample: Adding items to an Amazon shopping cart without being logged in. Amazon stores your cart ID in a cookie. When you close the tab and return tomorrow, the browser sends the cookie back, and Amazon restores your cart.

basic: Does the client (browser) have to manually write code to send a cookie back to the server in a `fetch` request?
intermediate: What happens if a user clears their browser cookies?

answers.question: Manually send?
answers.answer: No. The greatest feature of cookies is that the browser handles them completely automatically behind the scenes. Once set, the browser attaches them to every HTTP request to that specific domain.

answers.question: Clear cookies?
answers.answer: They instantly lose all active sessions (logged out of all websites) and lose all tracking preferences, because their browser throws away all the 'nametags'.
